en.name: Conversion of Saint Paul
en.summary: Commemorates the dramatic encounter on the road to Damascus that transformed Saul the persecutor into Paul the Apostle.
en.body: This feast commemorates the pivotal event recorded in the Acts of the Apostles in which Saul, a zealous persecutor of the early Christian Church actively traveling to Damascus to arrest believers, was struck to the ground by a blinding light and heard the voice of the risen Christ asking why he persecuted him, an encounter that left him temporarily blind and utterly transformed. After three days of blindness, prayer, and fasting, he was restored to sight, baptized, and began the missionary career that would make him the Church's most consequential early theologian and evangelist, traveling extensively across the Mediterranean world and authoring a substantial portion of the New Testament. The feast falls at the conclusion of the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity, a placement reflecting Paul's own later ministry of reconciling divided communities within the early Church.
